items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: The name 'Napoleon' appears only as a transcription artifact or misinterpretation of 'Mimile' (the poodle) or 'Coleman Hawkins' in the context of the jam session story. There is no evidence of a personal relationship with a person named Napoleon.

ctx.x:
was beautiful. He was handsome.

And he had a little club and he had a little poodle dog, you know, they called him Mimi. And little Mimi, when we got off, we went to (inaudible) place to meet our girlfriends, we'd meet each other.

There was another place we'd go is Budals, (phonetic). That was across the street from the post office. We would go there later anyway, see, we would go there later anyway.

So, Aikian's place was on, I think it was Rue -- well, I I said, Rue Perrier (phonetic) I know that -- and Rue…

-- Napoleon -- you don't feel it. You just feel good and Hawkins was building those castles and things -- and he was blowing and his little dog come right where he was and stood up and looked at Coleman Hawkins and then jumped up on the table.
Aikiam had to tell him, no, no, Mimile -- he said, no, I'm going to sit here and enjoy every bit of this. And she stayed there and Coleman Hawkins ran all of that stuff.
